title: Hidden offscreen labels lag badly while appearing when Stretch Mode is set to Canvas Items.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
Godot v4.6.1.stable, 4.5.stable, and 4.7 Dev 3 - macOS Tahoe (26.4.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M3 Max (Apple9) - Apple M3 Max (14 threads) - 36.00 GiB memory

Hardware: 
Macbook Pro - Apple M3 Max, 36 GB Ram, macOS Tahoe 26.4
(I can also reproduce this on an M1 MacBook Pro but have no other computers to test it on.)

### System information

macOS Tahoe (26.4.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M3 Max (Apple9) - Apple M3 Max (14 threads) - 36.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

There is a large lag spike when label nodes that are hidden and off-screen are set to visible for the first time. This seems to only happen when the Stretch Mode is set to "Canvas Items". If you change it to any other mode no lag spike happens. 

This also happens when built to device (computer, iPhones, and iPads in my case), it's not unique to the editor. Switching fonts does not help, turning off font effects makes no difference. 

### Steps to reproduce

It's best seen with the minimum reproduction project attached since most of it is in the level editor. 

1. In the MRP, load up the main scene.

2. Hold the right arrow key. You will encounter another sprite after a few seconds and notice the lag spike (it has to be arrow not "D" key, I kept the project as minimal as possible). 

Three key things have to happen for this lag spike: 
-The label has to be off screen initially.
-The label needs to be hidden initially.
-The Stretch Mode in Project Settings needs set to Canvas Items (it is by default in the MRP). 

If you switch the Stretch Mode to anything else, the lag won't happen. 

If you have the label unhidden in the scene inspector on launch, the lag won't happen.

Using modulate with an alpha instead of .visible makes no difference.

Putting the label on another z layer and changing layers makes no difference.

The project is as minimal as possible. It's just a player with an Area2D and an object with an Area2D using the _on_area_entered callback to detect a collision and set a label on the non-player object to visible. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26337288/issue.zip)

Also I don't know if this is helpful since I'm not super knowledgeable on Godot's profiler, but this is what the profiler shows whenever the lag spike happens: 

https://imgur.com/a/liLw7nL
